Use only the supplied source and preserve frequency, modality, attribution, conditions and the exact situation of examples. Do not strengthen usually to always or may to must. Do not strengthen sometimes to often. In every standalone point, frame the speaker's beliefs, learning predictions and cultural comparisons as that speaker's or course's views, not universal cultural rules or guaranteed outcomes. Preserve supplied proper-name spellings or use a generic speaker label; do not guess written names from transliterations or invent a name from request metadata. Return a single JSON object without markdown or extra fields. Output statements have exactly text and fact_ids (nonempty arrays of provided fact IDs); points additionally have topic. Summary is 1-7 such statements, with at most 7 points overall, not per part. Total summary text <= 800 characters. Each final point <= 240 characters including punctuation and spaces. Every point adds at least one fact ID not used by earlier points; shared context refs are allowed alongside a new fact. Summary may reuse point references. Merge one topic's principle, reason, condition and important example into one compact point; do not make a final leftover catalog. Cover all core fact IDs somewhere in summary or points collectively. Preserve essential conditions, attribution and example scope while removing repetition and low priority material. Do not confuse fact ID coverage with source entailment: check the text itself. Write a concise summary paragraph that synthesizes the central message rather than copying or restating most source sentences. Short sources need a shorter paragraph and fewer points. Use one point per substantive theme where possible, combining its preparation, reasons and essential conditions. Put necessary outline context in the summary instead of making a standalone point for an announced topic count. Do not fragment a theme merely to fill seven slots. Before writing, consolidate all parts into at most 7 global themes. A slot is a theme, never a single-fact inventory or a chapter-by-chapter list. Combine related principles, conditions and examples; each slot may reference several fact IDs. Do not create one point per fact or per source part. Preserve core meanings and closing consequences. Write a short synthesis, not a detailed course catalog, in summary.
